question: Which statement is NOT true about smooth muscles?
solution:
The correct answer is __**They have striations**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 

• **Smooth muscles** are also known as **non-striated** or **unstriped muscles** because they do not exhibit the **transverse bands** or **striations** seen in skeletal or cardiac muscles. This lack of striations is due to the absence of highly organized **sarcomeres**. *Hence, statement 4 is NOT true.* 

• These muscle cells are **uninucleate**, meaning each individual cell contains only **one** single, centrally located **nucleus**. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.* 

• **Smooth muscles** control **involuntary movements**, meaning they function automatically without **conscious effort**. Their activity is regulated by the **autonomic nervous system** and **hormones**. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.* 

• The structure of smooth muscle cells is **spindle-shaped** (also called **fusiform**), where the cells are thick in the middle and **tapered at both ends**. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.* 

• ***Hence, the correct answer is They have striations.*** 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

 

• **Location and Distribution:** 
 

• **Smooth muscles** are found in the walls of **hollow visceral organs**. Examples include the **stomach**, **intestines**, **urinary bladder**, **uterus**, and **gallbladder**. 

• They are also present in the **walls of blood vessels** (arteries and veins), where they regulate **blood pressure** by contracting or relaxing to change the vessel diameter. 

• They are found in the **respiratory tract**, **iris of the eye** (controlling pupil size), and the **arrector pili** muscles of the skin. 
 
 

• **Mechanism of Contraction:** 
 

• Unlike **skeletal muscles**, smooth muscles contract **slowly** but can maintain the **contraction** for a longer period without **fatigue**. 

• They use **actin** and **myosin** filaments for contraction, but these are arranged in a **loose network** rather than the rigid **sarcomere** structure, allowing the muscle to shorten significantly more than skeletal muscle. 
 
 

• **Comparison with Other Muscle Types:** 
 

• **Skeletal Muscle:** These are **striated**, **multinucleated**, and **voluntary** muscles attached to the skeleton. 

• **Cardiac Muscle:** These are **striated**, typically **uninucleate**, and **involuntary** muscles found only in the **heart**. They possess **intercalated discs** for rapid signal transmission. 
 
 

• **Key Biological Functions:** 
 

• In the **digestive system**, smooth muscles facilitate **peristalsis**, the wave-like contraction that moves **food** through the tract. 

• In the **urinary system**, they assist in the **expulsion of urine** from the body. 

• They play a vital role in **homeostasis** by controlling the **flow of fluids** and the **internal environment** of the body.
